item.title: Mice with human brain cells offer a tool to study disease. Ethicists ask: What's next?
item.description: Neuroscientists have made a major advance in modeling the human brain in mice, offering a new way to study conditions like cerebral palsy. Ethicists ask if it changes how these mice should be treated.

item.title: Senators question Trump's picks for top health positions, including surgeon general
item.description: On Wednesday, the Senate committee on health holds a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third attempt to nominate a surgeon general.

item.title: Air pollution spiked after the Trump administration stopped embassy monitoring
item.description: In 2025, the Trump administration ended a long-running program to collect air pollution data at U.S. embassies. A new study suggests that led to a 24-33% increase in local pollution levels.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Step, stand, stairs
item.description: When it comes to longevity, lots of research has shown how much you move matters. But a new study finds your pace may also be key -- even if you fall far short of daily step goals.

item.title: NPR looked for ChatGPT's new crisis feature. It's hard to find
item.description: Earlier this year, OpenAI launched a feature on ChatGPT meant to help people at risk of suicide connect with someone they trust for support. But its setup may prove challenging to someone in crisis.

item.title: Pennsylvania says an unvaccinated woman has died from measles-related complications
item.description: Pennsylvania has announced its third measles-related death in less than three weeks. A local coroner says the 40-year-old woman was unvaccinated.

item.title: Actor Tatyana Ali is advocating for Black and Indigenous maternal health
item.description: Actor Tatyana Ali says her healing journey after a traumatic childbirth has inspired her advocacy for Black maternal health, including support for midwives, doulas and other birth workers.

item.title: Black women are more likely to experience pregnancy trauma and have their pain ignored
item.description: Black mothers in the U.S. are three times as likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. Actress Tatyana Ali became an advocate after her own awful experience giving birth.
